extracted.intended_audience: readers and redistributors of Project Gutenberg eBooks (and general readers of The Sketch-Book)
extracted.subtask_description: Terms and practical requirements for using, copying, converting, distributing, or charging for Project Gutenberg electronic works, plus the author's brief meta-advice to readers and writers about variety, tolerance, and solicitude in authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominently display the Project Gutenberg sentence (1.E.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following sentence, with active links to, or other immediate access to, the full Project Gutenberg License must appear prominently whenever any copy of a Project Gutenberg work is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied or distributed:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "This eBook is for the use of anyone anywhere in the United States and most other parts of the world at no cost and with almost no restrictions whatsoever. You may copy it, give it away or re-use it under the terms of the Project Gutenberg™ License included with this eBook or online at www.gutenberg.org. If you are not located in the United States, you will have to check the laws of the country where you are located before using this eBook." (This sentence must be shown with active links or immediate access to the full license.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not remove or detach the full Project Gutenberg License (1.E.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not unlink or detach or remove the full Project Gutenberg License terms from this work, or any files containing a part of this work or any other work associated with Project Gutenberg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full license must remain attached to copies and derivative files; removing the license is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with 1.E.1–1.E.7 when distributing Project Gutenberg works (1.E general)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are redistributing or providing access to a work with the phrase 'Project Gutenberg' associated with or appearing on the work, you must comply with paragraphs 1.E.1 through 1.E.7 unless you obtain specific permission under paragraphs 1.E.8 or 1.E.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either follow the specified display, format, fee, and conversion rules (1.E.1–1.E.7) or obtain permission for alternative terms as described later in the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: If derived from public-domain texts in US, removing Project Gutenberg references permits freer copying (1.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual Project Gutenberg electronic work is derived from texts not protected by U.S. copyright law and you are located in the United States, the work can be copied and distributed without paying any fees or charges if all references to Project Gutenberg are removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation hopes users will keep the Project Gutenberg name associated with the work, but legally removing references to Project Gutenberg frees you from the Foundation's redistribution requirements for that copy in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must prominently display the license sentence when copying/displaying/performing (1.E.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not copy, display, perform, distribute or redistribute this electronic work, or any part of it, without prominently displaying the sentence set forth in paragraph 1.E.1 with active links or immediate access to the full terms of the Project Gutenberg License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any public access must include the required sentence and links; omission violates the license terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: When converting formats, provide original Plain Vanilla ASCII on request and include full license (1.E.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may convert and distribute this work in many formats, but if you provide access in any format other than the official 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' (or other official form), you must, at no additional cost, provide a copy or a way to obtain the original format upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any alternate format distributed must include the full Project Gutenberg License as specified in paragraph 1.E.1; you must provide a means to export or obtain the original official format without charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not charge a fee for access unless complying with fee provisions (1.E.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access to, viewing, displaying, performing, copying or distributing any Project Gutenberg works unless you comply with paragraph 1.E.8 or 1.E.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free distribution is the default; charging requires adherence to the specific royalty/permission provisions later in the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: If charging fees, pay royalties and follow reporting/payment rules (1.E.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may charge a reasonable fee for copies of or providing access to Project Gutenberg works provided that you pay a royalty fee of 20% of the gross profits you derive from the use of Project Gutenberg works, payable within 60 days following each date on which you prepare (or are legally required to prepare) your periodic tax returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional administrative and reporting requirements apply; the royalty is owed to the owner of the Project Gutenberg trademark and the paragraph contains further procedural detail (payment timing, calculation method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Country-specific copyright laws govern use (1.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The copyright laws of the place where you are located govern what you can do with this work; if you are outside the United States, check your country's laws in addition to the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation makes no representations concerning the copyright status of any work in any country other than the United States; compliance with local law is the user's responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works posted with copyright-holder permission carry additional terms (1.E.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual Project Gutenberg electronic work is posted with the permission of the copyright holder, your use and distribution must comply with both paragraphs 1.E.1 through 1.E.7 and any additional terms imposed by the copyright holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When permission has been granted by a rights holder, follow both Project Gutenberg's baseline rules and any extra constraints linked to that specific work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Gutenberg Foundation owns compilation copyright (1.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation owns a compilation copyright in the collection of Project Gutenberg electronic works; nearly all individual works in the collection are in the public domain in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While individual works may be public domain, the Foundation's compilation has rights; be mindful of both individual work status and compilation rights when redistributing collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite reader corrections (authorial request / Chaucer quote)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the book is wrong in any part, the reader is asked to call the author's attention to correct it: 'Where thou art wrong, after their help to call, Thee to correct in any part or all.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author explicitly requests readers' help in correcting errors and welcomes corrections to any part of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve miscellaneous/heterogeneous content for varied tastes (authorial strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the work is miscellaneous and written for different humors, it cannot be expected that any one reader will be pleased with the whole; if it contains something to suit each reader, the author's end is completely answered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author uses the metaphor of a varied table—different pieces will please different readers—and intentionally includes a mix of styles (ludicrous, pathetic, description, narrative) to reach diverse tastes rather than conforming to a single critic's counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be immobilized by conflicting critical advice (authorial counsel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author found contradictory but excellent advice (avoid the ludicrous; shun the pathetic; be tolerable at description but leave narrative alone; you lack a spirit of humor). To follow all such counsels would be to stand still.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When critics give mutually exclusive recommendations, the practical rule is not to attempt to satisfy all; instead, follow a consistent creative course (in this case, rambling on as begun) and provide variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask readers to tolerate what displeases them (reader tolerance request)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author requests that if the reader finds anything to dislike, they should 'tolerate it, as one of those articles which the author has been obliged to write for readers of a less refined taste.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit appeal to readers for indulgence regarding pieces included to serve other tastes—invites tolerance rather than strict judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge imperfections; persist and improve (author humility / craft principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author admits numerous faults and imperfections, lack of discipline in authorship, and diffidence from writing in a strange land, yet is encouraged to continue writing with the hope of acquiring steadier footing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-awareness and continued practice are presented as the route to improvement; solicitude to please should not paralyze creative effort.
